A sleuth-em-up where your tools are magic hacking tools and a keyboard. Overall a great experience, more user friendly and forgiving than other hacking simulators, but still keeps you on your toes. 

A few complaints, by the end of the game there ends up being a huge list of computers you can access. This clutters up the screen quite a bit, especially with the expansion nodes added in there. Also a few things end up a bit tedious, like running shells over and over and the notes "app" taking up a lot of memory (the in game reason for it is amazing though).

Being a fan of the older Uplink game, I have always kept an eye out for modern "hacking" games.  I saw quite a few positive reviews for this and I decided to test it out.  My only regret is that I didn't  just get the Ultimate Bundle.  But I think I will still even with the base game already in my library.

If you want to try yourself in the role of a hacker, this game will certainly capture your attention. A wonderful design, soundtrack, plot, fabulous range of emotions… all this makes you feel like a professional hacker!

I don't see what the big fuss is about. OK so I can get that making a hacking game is a challenging problem, but this really gives you an idea of what it's like to be a scriptkiddie, not a hacker. Also as a daily user of Linux I found the incomplete (not to mention renamed) shell commands to be extremely frustrating!

In addition I found the gameplay very repetitive. For the vast majority of the game it was: get an IP, run some scripts against the defenses. Look through /home, rince and repeat.
We are all script kiddies now.
Solid game, linux commandline isnt quite bash but it was fun none the less.

Turn down the lights, bask in your monitor glow and type away exaggerratingly fast, enjoy pretending to be really skilled and technical. 

Worked for me anyway....
Help the dead man to fulfill his revenge.

Super fun and unique hacking game with great base mechanics (based off real Unix commands) and extensions to keep you entertained for hours.

The base game revolves around you hacking into and digging through a bunch of simulated computer systems to uncover the truth about some information you get from a hacker who just died. You join a faction (or two if you're clever) along the way who have missions for you to complete to rank up with them, which gives you new tools to use to explore the virtual world. The story is a lot of fun and ends with a bang.

Soundtrack is really enjoyable.
Graphics are convincing and a good mix of GUI and command line elements.

DLC is a great addition to the game and I'd definetly reccomend it.

The developer makes it really easy to learn and make extensions in this game, which has led to a bunch of awesome extensions being developed which add hours of exciting playtime.

5/5, one of the best hacking games I've ever played. If you even think that you'd be interested in this game or this genere, you should try it out.
It's fun now and then - not too challenging in the beginning though.

Hacknet is a simulated hacking simulator (well done me for pointing out the obvious.) where you have a Linux type of interface, your objectives generally come out as
>Connect to pc
>Probe it for ports
>Hack it
>Do something that a client wants you to do
>Job done
It does take a little practice getting my head around using the commands, but the train starts rolling the more you get used to it. Not necessarily a game aimed at the young, in the sense that this can be very complicated in parts here and there, so in reality, it's aimed at people who have a good understanding of using the terminal in a Linux based operating system or CMD in Windows.
Brief but enjoyable. Really captures the feel of "visiting" somebody else's system. Prior UNIX experience is helpful but not required.
This game is so good. It is not hard to learn!!!.

Think of this game as a modern day text base adventure.  I am completely and uttering enjoying this game.  Racing against the clock to get the objective solved.  Getting angry and plotting my revenge on the intruders of my system.  Anticipating the revenge that I'm going to enact on the system of the intruders.  Starts you off with simple tools and works you into more complex ones.  Even the little things like breaking into a system and finding a new x-server interface theme to try.  Get excited when I see a new one of those:  can't wait to see what it looks like.  A warning must be given:  YOU WILL LOSE TRACK OF TIME WHILE PLAYING THIS GAME!  :)

To the creators of this game I tip my hat to you good people.  :)

Honestly? This is exactly the kind of hacking sim I was looking for when I found it. It's been a while, I played through, didn't play through it again for a while, but I recently came back around to it and now I'm just hooked all over again, especially with the option of extensions. It's just a lot of fun to play, makes me feel like a total badass.

Looked at the commands.

Went to my computer in-game.

Typed in, "openCDTray".

Scared the crap out of me as I almost had a heart attack.

10/10 game. Would recommend.

I enjoyed this game a lot. I am in the IT field (software development), so due to my background it was a lot of fun playing a computer hacking game. While real hacking I'm sure is quite sophisticated, it was interesting to get a glimpse of what it might be like.

What I really enjoyed was the ongoing mystery/thriller narrative. The pacing was pretty good and the game took me roughly 17 hours with breaks that may have driven up the length. The length overall felt just right.

To play this game you have to be ok with a lot of reading, and it is required to pick up clues and understand what's going on, and typing in order to enter commands. It is also helpful to write down some of the commands you learn or to follow a guide along the way in case you get stuck (which happened to me a few times). The writing uses humor and some tense timed moments to keep things interesting. Overall, I enjoyed this quite a lot and would recommend it.

Hacknet is a unique game that mixed pseudo-linux command line game play in a simulated tale about a hacker's last request (not the player). You navigate an increasingly complex web of story elements to get to the heart of the story, and ultimately, the final hacking showdown which is reminiscent of playing Neuromancer (video game) and fighting against Wintermute. (Spoiler [spoiler]there is no artificial intelligence in this game.[/spoiler])

Since I was methodical about good hacking hygene (always deleting the logs of your activities from every server you touch) and because I trapped the one side-story villain (and accidentally deleted the logs of the attack, thus preventing myself from getting the side [spoiler]/el[/spoiler] storyline), I finished the game in only 4 hours.

While the story elements are pretty decent, and the game play is unique (being command line based)-- there were some moments in the game that can only be described as "waiting simulators" (specifically, you get the ability to decrypt files-- and if you want to wade through the wealth of story files available you can easily spent over an hour just decrypting & deleting files.) Being able to script/automate certain things would have been an improvement over the existing gameplay (or even just a speed up mode to bypass the artificial decryption delay.)

But aside from that frustration, I thought pretty highly of the gameplay--

But when it's going to only be about 6-8 hours of gameplay for $10-- I think it's over priced.  The game really needed a lot more story content (not chasing minutae down the rabbit hole-- but actually more story, more "missions" and so forth.)

But at $4, I think it's money well spent.


Recommendation: Buy on sale.

[b]Hacknet[/b] is a hacking simulation game. You are probably familiar with other games of the same genre, such as Uplink and the Hacker Evolution series. This game is, I dare to say, better than both of those, despite having some bugs.
If this review is too long for you, I suggest you to only read the first paragraph about the game's content and the final verdict at the end.

[h1] What is happening in the game: [/h1]
Fourteen days after Agent Bit's disappearance, a failsafe sequence was activated. You are one of the only people who can solve Bit's death. As you get more and more involved into the hacker community, you start unveiling a mystery and it's up to you to discover what was really behind Bit and the security system he created.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*]After the success of Uplink, there had to be a game sooner or later that would try to improve what Uplink started. Hacknet not only achieves that, but takes it to the next level. The story alone is amazing and makes sure that you're not just repeating the same commands and actions over and over but gives it a meaning.
[*]I have to say that the whole interface is working really nicely when it comes to clarity and effectiveness. You can do 90% of things both in the Display section and Terminal section, but they are both placed in the interface and I find it surprisingly effective. I use the Display section for figuring out what is going on and the Terminal section to execute commands.
[*]You have a nice map on the bottom of the screen, that is showing all of the cyber locations you have visited already. As you get to connect to tons of computers, you would think that the map would be overcrowded, but this is not the case. I found the map really useful, despite it being almost completely covered.
[*]There is no bouncing from servers as you remember from other hacking games. Instead, traces are lost if you simply disconnect. Even better is the way how the developers managed what happens if you get traced. Your computer (the virtual one, of course) activates a failsafe sequence. It tells you the IP of your ISP and your IP. You have to break into your ISP's server in a very limited amount of time and from there, reset your IP. This is a brilliant way to prevent accidental game overs and having to start all over again. Instead, you are provided with one more hard (and fun) challenge.
[*]I really enjoy the soundtrack in this game. The song was written by a guy who also made the soundtrack for Hotline Miami. The music matches with the tension of your current illegal doings and really makes your heart beat faster. Amazing job.
[*]The in-game hacking is based on actual UNIX commands, which is pretty cool. Still, don't expect to be a pro hacker when you finish this game. You would still be a few steps away, the first step being stopping playing hacking simulators instead of learning the real deal.
[*]There is a ton of Easter Eggs in this game. A clicker game, hidden Steam keys and a lot more. [*]It's really impressive how they manage to fit all sorts of things into this game. Also, you should read all of the IRC chat logs when you encounter them. They can be super funny (and useful).
[*]I have cooperated with the developer in bug-related issues and I have to say that I really like the way that the developer interacts with the community. (Almost) all of the bugs I have encountered were fixed and I'm glad that they managed to bring the final release in a shape that they did.
[*]Another interesting aspect of this game is puzzle solving. You have to think really hard to solve some of them and you even have to remember things from your previous missions, write things down and stuff like that.
[*]If you don't like the user interface, you will encounter skins later in the game that you can download and make your virtual computer looks just the way you want.
[*]The system requirements are low, which is great for old computers. However, there are some moments when FPS suddenly drops and gets to a normal level quickly.
[*]$/€10 is a steal for a game of such quality. If you ever enjoyed hacking games, this should be the top game on your wishlist.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
Bugs. Many were fixed, but some are still present. The game-breaking ones are gone, however, so you should be fine.
This game should have a button to reset progress. I wanted to do that a couple of times but you can't really do that without browsing through folders and files.

[h1]The final verdict:[/h1]
As a big fan of hacking games, I was very happy to be able to play Hacknet. The game is certainly made well and definitely recommend this game to you if you enjoy hacking games as well. The story is surprisingly good and adds an important part to the whole experience. The hacking really feels real and, even though that the commands are pretty much the same through the whole game, never feel repetitive.
This is, no doubt, the best hacking game ever released. Get it, and fast!

Hacknet precisely strikes an engaging balance between accessibility and authenticity.  Many other 'hacking' games focus on realism, technicality, and PVP-focused experiences centered around collecting cash and upgrading.  Hacknet, in contrast, is a narrative-driven adventure game told through the vehicle of networks and software.  It's a very different experience from the other stuff out there.

Hacknet begins by thrusting you into a mystery.  A fellow hacker will ask you to look into a matter, sending you down the road of your adventure.  Along the way, you'll have to take on contract work to build reputation with various factions, face adversarial hackers, break into corporate mainframes, and more.  Contracts range from silly to grave, following certain threads of exploration can grant you additional insight or early access to tools you'd have to wait much longer to reach.

Hacking is not realistic, although it is loosely based on unix-like commands and conventions.  Most PCs you encounter will have a selection of defenses that require the use of specific programs to bypass them.  Your PC has limited memory and each program uses a bit of it, so hacking is generally a function of optimizing your hack time by learning which programs use more RAM and how long each one takes.  By understanding your tools, you can breach defenses rapidly, allowing you to break in, steal files, and leave before active tracers can find your PC and force a reboot.  

Due to it's emphasis on storytelling, there may not be much replayability, but the community workshop extensions help with that.  Dozens of user-created storylines have been made using Hacknet's framework, and tools are available to create your own.

I can't recommend this game enough to anyone who has even a passing interest.  If you saw this and found yourself intrigued, this is the game to try.  My only regret is that I can't find any other games that come close.

I was blown away by Hacknet from the first moment the game started through the very end.  I didn't think it was going to be anything special, but the story, the puzzles, before you know it you're embroiled in a deepening mystery that will take all of your cunning to solve, and all of your skills to set things right.  Great music and unexpected visuals accompany the gameplay too, and the commands are simplified enough so as not to completely overwhelm the UNIX newbs.  Overall I give this a solid 9/10.

scan   -- finds other connected servers
scp <filename>   -- downloads files to your home IP
rm *   --remove all files in directory

shell    --create tool to hack proxies and trap hackers
reboot   --reboots server
analyze   --analyzes firewall, next command cracks it

porthack  --crack ports 
webserverworm 80   --crack HTTP port
smtpoverflow 25   --crack SMTP port
ftpbounce 21   --crack FTP port
sql_memcorrupt 1433  --crack SQL port
sshcrack  -- crack SSH port
